criteria.description: On every request for a given IP, the per-IP timestamp array must be filtered to remove entries older than 60 seconds before the count is compared against MAX_REQUESTS. The pruning must occur inline on each request, not via a background interval.
criteria.evidence: rateLimiter.ts line 22: `const timestamps = (store.get(ip) ?? []).filter(ts => now - ts < WINDOW_MS);` — the filtered array is used for both the `timestamps.length >= MAX_REQUESTS` check (line 24) and `store.set(ip, timestamps)` (line 31). No background interval exists. pnpm test: 2 test files, 21 tests, all passed.

criteria.description: When a 429 response is returned, the Retry-After response header must equal the computed number of whole seconds until the oldest in-window timestamp will fall outside the 60-second window, rounded up. Specifically: Math.ceil((oldestTimestamp + WINDOW_MS - now) / 1000). The value must not be hardcoded.
criteria.evidence: rateLimiter.ts line 25: `const retryAfter = Math.ceil((timestamps[0] + WINDOW_MS - now) / 1000);` — uses `timestamps[0]` (oldest in-window timestamp after filtering) and `WINDOW_MS`, not a hardcoded literal. No literal `60` appears as the retryAfterSeconds argument. pnpm test: 21/21 passed.

criteria.description: A GET /health request must bypass the rate-limit check entirely and call next() without incrementing the IP's request count. The exemption check must compare req.path against '/health' (with leading slash).
criteria.evidence: rateLimiter.ts lines 14-17: `if (req.path === '/health') { next(); return; }` — uses the string literal `'/health'` with leading slash. The early return occurs before any store read or timestamp push. pnpm test: 21/21 passed.
